title: every digit is sorted exactly once — a machine-checked theorem of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit
description:
every digit is sorted exactly once, declared in src/proof/coin.lean and accepted by the Lean 4 kernel, sorry-free and axiom-free, closing by by decide.

Statement (Lean):

digits.all (fun d => (tetB.contains d && tetB.contains (refl d)) || (tetA.contains d && axis.contains (refl d)) || (axis.contains d && tetA.contains (refl d)) || (refl d == d) || (refl d > 9))

Statement (LaTeX):

\forall d \in \mathrm{digits},\; d \in \mathrm{tetB} \land \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) \in \mathrm{tetB} \lor d \in \mathrm{tetA} \land \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) \in \mathrm{axis} \lor d \in \mathrm{axis} \land \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) \in \mathrm{tetA} \lor \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) = d \lor \mathrm{refl}\mathopen{}\left(d\right) > 9

What this record establishes. A dated, public, citable deposit of this declaration and its proof, recomputable from the source it names. That is priority. It is not a claim that the result is unknown to the literature: prior art for this file is recorded in src/proof/priorart.lean as unclassified — no prior-art search has been performed, so no novelty is asserted.

Scope. The declaration is decided over a finite domain by exhaustion. It settles no Clay Millennium Problem and claims no quantum speedup. 0/7.
